declared_proposition: Let f be a real essentially bounded function on the unit circle and let a_r be its Fourier coefficients. Every finite Hermitian Toeplitz section T_N=(a_(i-j)) satisfies ||T_N||_op<=||f||_infinity. Therefore a whitened core margin delta survives whenever ||f||_infinity<delta. Absolute summability of the coefficients is not necessary.
mathematical_argument: For x in C^N and p_x(z)=sum_j x_j z^j, the Toeplitz quadratic form is x* T_N x=integral f(theta)|p_x(exp(i theta))|^2 dtheta/(2 pi). Its absolute value is at most ||f||_infinity||x||_2^2. For f(theta)=C sign(cos theta), a_(plus/minus(2k+1))=2C(-1)^k/[pi(2k+1)]. The absolute coefficient sum diverges, while every finite section remains bounded by C.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: TICKET-178's summable absolute profile is sufficient but not necessary. A bounded signed Fourier symbol can control every finite section even when absolute row sums diverge. This does not construct the actual pole-neutral Weil symbol or prove its norm lies below the core margin.

discarded_route: absolute summability of the signed Weil tail as a necessary condition for uniform Toeplitz control
remaining_gap: No arithmetic construction identifies the actual pole-neutral whitened Weil tail with a bounded real Fourier symbol whose essential supremum is below the core margin.
claim_boundary: No RH proof or zero exclusion; one exact phase-sensitive Toeplitz certificate and one nonsummable bounded-symbol counterfamily only.
